overview: White takes the c-pawn and Black normally regains it with ...e6 and ...Bxc5, or ...Nf6 and ...Na6/...Nxc5, so material returns. The positions that result are open and close to a symmetrical or Queen's Gambit-type game. It is a rare line; I am unsure which branch is the main line.

white_ideas.idea: Hold the pawn with b4 or Nf3 and Nc3, or give it back for a development lead
Develop quickly with e4, Nc3 and Bf4/Be3, taking a small centre

black_ideas.idea: Regain the pawn with ...e6 and ...Bxc5 or ...Na6 and ...Nxc5
Play for ...d5 with free development and a symmetrical, active position

typical_structures.structure: Open symmetrical-like position after the c-pawn is regained, or a Queen's Gambit-type centre

character.notes: Not forcing; no early tactics beyond regaining the pawn.

gambit.notes: Black regains the c5 pawn by force with ...e6 and ...Bxc5 or ...Na6, so no lasting gambit.

soundness.notes: Sound; Black regains material without trouble.

structure.notes: Centre not decided after the pawn is regained.

approach.notes: Played now and then by strong players.

level.notes: Plans are straightforward and theory is minimal.

sublines_that_differ.name: 2...e6 3.e4
sublines_that_differ.how: Black regains the pawn with an active bishop; White has the e4 centre.

character.reason: Material comes back and play is open but not especially forcing.

gambit.reason: Black regains the pawn at once, so it is not a lasting gambit.

soundness.reason: Black regains the pawn without risk.

structure.reason: The centre is undecided after the exchange.

approach.reason: Less common but not an unusual choice for strong players.

level.reason: Plans are simple and there is little theory.

plans.reason: Position can go several ways and no plan dominates.
